item.title: Apple may have found room for MagSafe in its impossibly thin foldable iPhone (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone—widely expected to be called the iPhone Ultra—will likely support MagSafe despite its extremely thin design. If true, it would give Apple an advantage over Samsung's foldables, which require cases for magnetic charging. Other rumored features include a titanium body, an advanced crease-reducing hinge, split-screen multitasking, and a price above $2,000.

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro leaks suggest photographers are finally getting the feature they've been waiting for (2 minute read)
item.description: While the foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to dominate headlines, the iPhone 18 Pro may be the more significant upgrade for photographers thanks to a rumored variable-aperture camera lens that could offer greater control over depth of field and image quality. Combined with reports of a larger battery—up to 5,500 mAh on the Pro Max—the device could become Apple's most capable photography-focused iPhone yet, despite an otherwise familiar design.

item.title: Adobe Brings Image, Video, and PDF Creation Directly into Slack (1 minute read)
item.description: Adobe for Slack brings image, video, and PDF creation into Slack, letting Slackbot turn conversations and files into polished content without leaving the workspace. Slackbot reads context from conversations, Canvases, and shared files, then routes requests to more than 70 connected Adobe tools. It requires a qualifying Slack plan, Business+ or Enterprise+, plus a separate Adobe subscription.

item.title: The Most Exciting and Exhausting Time to Be a Designer (6 minute read)
item.description: Designers are now expected to be technically fluent in AI tooling and world-class in craft at once, two full-time jobs whose bars are rising together. The exhaustion has two sources: mistaking engineering velocity for the right ruler, and a feed running on a constant drip of weekend prototypes. Judgment is becoming the scarce resource, and the designers who come out strongest will be rested enough to do it.

item.title: Feeling Ignored? Here's What to Do (2 minute read)
item.description: Being ignored is one of the hardest situations designers face, but rejection is rarely a dead end for the idea itself. Curiosity beats the ego trap: ask whether others were rejected too, whether the timing was right, and which tradeoffs the decision-maker had to balance. People agree to ideas based on trust more than merit, so asking for feedback beats cataloging a coworker's limitations.

item.title: My View on Design Engineering (6 minute read)
item.description: A design engineer's real role isn't simply being a designer who codes or a developer with design skills—it's owning product coherence across the gap between design and development. As AI makes creating interfaces faster, the biggest challenge becomes maintaining consistency, handling edge cases, refining interactions, and making the countless judgment calls that determine whether a product feels polished and intentional rather than fragmented. Ultimately, design engineers act as translators, custodians of quality, and curators of taste, ensuring the shipped product remains cohesive even as teams, tools, and codebases evolve.

item.title: Spec Driven Design — From logic to style (7 minute read)
item.description: In the later stages of Spec-Driven Design, designers first define a visual direction through moodboards and written style guides, then use AI agents to apply those styles to working prototypes, and finally refine the results until they match the original vision. The process emphasizes maintaining designer control: AI accelerates implementation, but human judgment remains responsible for selecting references, defining aesthetics, and ensuring quality. Refinement can happen through prompting AI, editing designs in Figma with code-linked workflows, or directly modifying code, with the goal of achieving a polished, pixel-perfect product rather than accepting AI-generated approximations.

item.title: Design Systems That Get Used (5 minute read)
item.description: Everyone plans for the difficulty of building a design system that scales, and almost nobody plans for how hard it is to get people to use one. Adoption comes down to three fits every time: the organization, the products the system has to serve, and a team equipped to sustain it. A technically excellent system misaligned with those three sits unused, and the mistake costs twice: once to build it and once to replace it.

item.title: rbl rebrands University of East Anglia around ‘Original By Nature' ethos (2 minute read)
item.description: The University of East Anglia has unveiled a new brand identity built around the idea “Original by Nature,” aiming to reconnect the institution with its history of independent thinking, creative innovation, and environmental leadership. Developed after extensive consultation with students, staff, and stakeholders, the rebrand introduces a refined visual system inspired by the Norfolk landscape, a stronger verbal identity, and a more cohesive strategy designed to support the university's national and international ambitions.

item.title: This 3D Artist Uses Unreal Engine 5 and Blender to Achieve Incredible Detail in Heroic Character Designs (1 minute read)
item.description: 3D artist Andres Zambrano works in ZBrush, Maya, Substance Painter, Marvelous Designer, Unreal Engine 5, and Blender, chasing handcrafted detail and dramatic lighting on heroic figures.

item.title: The Website Design Secret Nobody Tells You (Until It's Already Cost You) (15 minute read)
item.description: Visitors decide whether they trust a site in about 0.05 seconds, long before a single word gets read, and copy rarely undoes that snap judgment.

item.title: Try Google Pics: Easy Image Creation and Editing in Google Workspace (2 minute read)
item.description: Google Pics, an image creation and editing tool built on the Nano Banana model, reaches Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and most Workspace business customers. Object segmentation, in-image text editing and translation, and collaborative editing give precise control over an image rather than regenerating it from scratch. Integration is available in Docs and Slides, with Drive arriving in the coming weeks.

item.title: Updates to Generative Plugins and Shaders (1 minute read)
item.description: Custom generative plugins and shaders, built by prompting the Figma agent, gain animated and interactive shaders that respond to motion and mouse input. Creations can now be published to the Community or to an organization, and a code viewer exposes the underlying shader and plugin code. MCP updates let third-party agents modify plugins and shaders, with shaders rendering correctly in generated React code.

item.title: Leakers battle over whether third iPhone 18 Pro color will be silver or black (1 minute read)
item.description: Leaks continue to point to Dark Cherry/Burgundy and Sky Blue as two of the iPhone 18 Pro's launch colors. The main uncertainty is the third finish, with some well-known leakers claiming Apple will offer black while others believe silver is more likely. Until Apple's announcement next week, both options remain plausible, though recent reports suggest silver and black are the final contenders.

item.title: Ecosystem Design (6 minute read)
item.description: Ecosystem design pushes past the product boundary, shaping the conditions and capabilities people need to succeed on a platform rather than the interface itself. Integrations, partnerships, marketplaces, developer platforms, community development, and corporate development are the six surfaces where a product becomes a world other people build on. Five practices follow: design the whole customer loop, treat third parties as users with business models, build trust, tend community, and treat docs as a product.

item.title: AI Is Making Product Development Faster. But Where Did the Work Go? (11 minute read)
item.description: AI can dramatically speed up individual tasks like research synthesis, prototyping, and code generation, but that doesn't automatically make the entire product development process faster. Often the work doesn't disappear—it shifts into review, verification, refactoring, or downstream teams, creating hidden costs that can erode the initial gains. The real question isn't whether AI increases local productivity, but whether it improves the whole system's ability to turn ideas into reliable products without accumulating technical debt, instability, or rework.

item.title: Is Product Discovery a Phase or a Weekly Habit? (18 minute read)
item.description: Product discovery works as weekly customer touchpoints by the team building the product, not as a kickoff phase that hands a backlog to engineering. Discovery and delivery are two kinds of work on one team, and a high kill rate is the test that discovery is real. Recruiting is the bottleneck: a Monday-to-Friday cadence survives only when a conversation is already on the calendar, even a customer-support ride-along.

item.title: On Animating What You Can't See (4 minute read)
item.description: A ghosted double image in DuckDuckGo for iOS's floating toolbar survived three rounds of retiming because the bug was view ownership, not animation timing. Recording the transition at 60fps and stepping through it with ffmpeg showed the tab-count badge fully visible 24 frames before the snapshot animation began. Two failure modes generalize: snapshotting a view's bounds instead of what it draws, and resizing a snapshot instead of scaling it.

item.title: René Bieder's Neurath X is a geometric typeface made for the age of AI (4 minute read)
item.description: A new typeface family explores how far geometric reduction can be pushed without sacrificing readability, drawing inspiration from early modernist experiments in typography and visual communication. Built as both proportional and monospaced families with extensive stylistic alternates, it reimagines the unrealized radical potential of classics like Futura while balancing mathematical purity with practical usability. The release extends beyond the typeface itself through a coordinated visual identity of 3D animation, motion design, and sound, all expressing the same philosophy of clarity, reduction, and geometric transformation.

item.title: The new Disney World logo design is actually kind of genius (1 minute read)
item.description: Disney World's upcoming 55th-anniversary logo is earning praise for cleverly combining two “5”s into unmistakable Mickey Mouse ears while reviving elements of the resort's original 1971 globe logo. Fans have responded far more positively than they did to the 50th-anniversary mark, praising its simplicity, nostalgia, and stronger visual concept.

item.title: Art&Graft's In Pursuit of Magic is a Reminder of Why We Do This at All (6 minute read)
item.description: In Pursuit of Magic took the London studio Art&Graft two years and 42 people, all answering one question: what is the pursuit of magic for you?

item.title: Sand Castle Artist Elevates a Classic Beach Activity into Unbelievable Art and Architecture (1 minute read)
item.description: Sand Castle University, founded in 2017 and now staffed by five instructors, turns a childhood beach pastime into architectural sculpture packed with windows, brickwork, and staircases.

item.title: How illustrator Azra Hirji turns the family table into an archive of food, migration and memory (3 minute read)
item.description: Illustrator Azra Hirji creates colorful, food-filled scenes inspired by family, culture, migration, and shared meals, turning personal memories and global influences into a distinctive visual style.

item.title: AI Videos Displace Chinese Actors and Livestreamers (1 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated videos are rapidly displacing human actors, influencers, and livestreamers across China's entertainment industry, with productions already substituting digital performers for real ones. In Q1 2026, roughly 128,000 short dramas were published, triple all of 2025's output. One minute of AI video now costs just $90-$120, about a tenth of human-actor production costs, and some performers must digitize their voice and likeness before being let go.

item.title: OpenAI Drops Cursor Partnership Over SpaceX Distrust (2 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI will cut off Cursor's access to its models on November 12, two weeks after SpaceX completed its $60 billion acquisition of the coding tool's parent company. The stated reason is trust rather than technology, citing prior contract violations by Elon Musk's companies. Cursor now leans harder on Anthropic's Claude and its in-house Composer model.

item.title: Apple Finds “Shocking Evidence” in Ex-Employee's MacBook (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple says new forensic evidence from a former engineer's laptop strengthens its trade-secret theft lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that ex-employee Chang Liu used confidential Apple engineering files in his OpenAI work, discussed the unauthorized data access internally, instructed a colleague to destroy evidence during Apple's investigation, and worked with a tool sharing the name of an internal Apple application—claims Apple argues justify accelerated discovery because the alleged trade secrets may already have been incorporated into AI systems.

item.title: How Brand Design Builds Trust (9 minute read)
item.description: Visual identity shapes judgments of credibility within seconds, giving typography, layout and consistency a direct role in whether audiences trust a brand. Six principles are set out with brand examples, covering decision-focused design, visual consistency, visible proof, familiar patterns, transparent information architecture and verifiable detail. Each comes with implementation steps designers can apply to a current project.

item.title: How Do You Measure AI's Impact on Design? (6 minute read)
item.description: Figma launched a multi-year study in 2024 to track AI's impact on design and product development, using AI tools to help conduct the research itself. The company built a sentiment-based AI impact index, ran 639 AI-moderated interviews analyzed through a custom thematic-analysis tool, and created a shared dashboard for cross-functional reporting. In 2026, the index reached 62 out of 100 points, nearly double its 2024 level, with every measured dimension exceeding the prior year's expectations.

item.title: Why Users Experience Interfaces Differently (23 minute read)
item.description: A UX designer reflects on a painful realization that even well-tested designs often fail in the real world because designers suffer from the curse of knowledge, ignore users' real-world contexts, design against users' mental models, overlook accessibility realities, and treat usability testing as validation rather than discovery. The solution is to design with humility, involve diverse users early, test in realistic conditions, and focus on how people actually experience products rather than how designers intend them to work.

item.title: Design Has Outgrown the Traditional Designer (6 minute read)
item.description: Design programs still recruit artistically inclined students, but the profession now demands research, systems thinking, ethics, and product strategy alongside visual craft. US labor projections show graphic design employment falling 2 percent through 2035 while web and digital interface roles grow 6 percent. Admissions and teaching should therefore weigh reasoning and defensible decisions, not portfolios alone.

item.title: How Brands Stand Out by Breaking Category Conventions (5 minute read)
item.description: The most distinctive brands often gain an advantage by borrowing ideas, behaviors, and experiences from entirely different industries rather than following the conventions of their own category. Examples ranging from Liquid Death and Lego to hospitality-inspired retail experiences show that innovation comes from remixing unexpected influences, creating memorable moments, and challenging category norms while remaining true to a clear brand purpose. As categories become increasingly blurred, brands that look beyond their competitors and embrace experimentation are more likely to stand out, build stronger emotional connections, and avoid the trap of becoming interchangeable with everyone else.

item.title: What Component Specs Leave Behind (10 minute read)
item.description: Looping "round trip" tests—generating specs from Figma, rendering them back, and diffing the results—reveal what design-to-code contracts silently drop, distort, or invent. The exercise exposed hidden assumptions, transformation bugs, and schema gaps in one such tool, while also clarifying which Figma features, like custom prop ordering or motion, can't or won't be supported. Round trips rarely converge to zero difference, but they let teams precisely name what's lost versus intentionally excluded, improving contract quality.

item.title: Five Design Tools Worth Buying on Amazon (7 minute read)
item.description: Five inexpensive design tools bought on Amazon are reviewed against a single test: whether they get picked up again within a week.

item.title: Designers Are Fixing Terrible AI Flyers (1 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated flyers have spread across small businesses, replacing the folk design tradition built in Photoshop and Microsoft Paint.

item.title: A redesigned Apple Watch now seems further in the future (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to be modest upgrades focused on new ceramic case options and improved health tracking, including continuous heart-rate monitoring and more insightful wellness software, while a major redesign remains in development and could arrive in 2027 or be delayed until 2028.

item.title: Instagram Will Demote AI-generated Influencers if They Don't Clearly Label Their Account (2 minute read)
item.description: Instagram now requires profiles featuring AI-generated personas to use a new "AI-generated profile" label, replacing the previous optional "AI creator" tag. Accounts that don't apply the label to AI-generated people will face reduced reach, though appeals are possible through the Account Status dashboard. The change targets only AI persona accounts specifically, not broader AI-generated content, amid rising concern over misleading AI "influencers" impersonating real humans.

item.title: Alibaba Launches Wan3.0 AI Video Model after $10 Billion Share Sale (1 minute read)
item.description: Alibaba officially rolled out Wan3.0, an upgraded AI video-generation model, a day after announcing a $10 billion share placement to fund rising AI spending. The model generates 30-second videos from documents, spreadsheets, slides, and web pages, and has been used since its August 6 public beta. The share sale is the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company, coming after Alibaba reported a 75% plunge in quarterly earnings due to soaring AI capital expenditure.

item.title: Workflow Lab: Moving between Design and Code with Agents (5 minute read)
item.description: Figma's MCP server and Code Connect give coding agents access to a team's components, tokens, and layouts, so generated code matches design specs. In the example workflow, a developer diagrams the flow in FigJam, reuses existing components, and catches token drift before review.

item.title: How AI-Ready is Your Design System? Now You Can Measure It. (15 minute read)
item.description: open-design-system-bench is an open benchmark measuring whether AI coding agents use a design system correctly when generating UI. Four systems scored between 52.2 and 63.4 on its AI-readiness composite, and none reached the AI-native tier. Across 898 graded generations, some models ignored the design system entirely while others hallucinated component names.

item.title: The Custodial Era of UX: Cleaning Up After AI (10 minute read)
item.description: AI is pushing UX into a “custodial era” where teams can generate and ship features faster than they can properly evaluate them, creating UX debt. As a result, UX practitioners increasingly act as custodians who clean up, simplify, validate, and triage AI-generated experiences, helping organizations distinguish what can be built from what should be built, while adapting research and evaluation processes to keep pace with rapid production and embedding UX principles directly into AI generation workflows to prevent future problems.

Illustrator's Text to Vector tool generates genuinely editable SVG paths rather than raster images, a capability no major competing AI tool offers.

item.title: The new CD Projekt Red logo just sparked the weirdest backlash graphic design has ever seen (3 minute read)
item.description: CD Projekt Red has refreshed its firebird logo with sharper, more aggressive features and a stronger use of red to better reflect the mythological Slavic raróg it represents, but despite the redesign being a relatively modest evolution, some social media users have bizarrely interpreted the shift to a black-and-red color scheme as a political statement, even though the company says the update is simply intended to create a more modern, confident, energetic, and culturally authentic brand identity.

item.title: Design's Legibility Gap (4 minute read)
item.description: Design's struggle for legitimacy stems from "legibility," where organizations only value predictable, determinate work they can measure and plan around. Unlike engineering or marketing, UX/Design remained a synthetic, indeterminate practice, making its core work—research, iteration, and conceptual modeling—invisible to organizations. Design leadership's real challenge, then, is not translating design to the business, but expanding what businesses recognize as legitimate, valuable work.

item.title: Nope, the new Apple Mac mini ad isn't AI – and there's a delightful BTS video to prove it (1 minute read)
item.description: Apple's new Mac mini stop-motion ad celebrates human craftsmanship with handmade clay animation, positioning the computer as a tool that enhances rather than replaces creativity.

item.title: This Rebrand of a Voice-Journaling App Looks Lovely, but is an 'AI Illustration System' the Right Call? (4 minute read)
item.description: The Working Assembly's new identity for voice-journaling app Untold centers on a bespoke AI illustration system trained to feel emotionally resonant rather than algorithmically generated.

item.title: Moriz Oberberger's bendy figures and whimsical cartoons reveal “the strange beauty of ordinary situations” (1 minute read)
item.description: Illustrator and animator Moriz Oberberger creates playful yet subtly unsettling artwork featuring awkward characters, unusual proportions, and expressive mark-making, using experimental drawing and painting techniques to explore vulnerability, tension, and the strange beauty hidden within everyday situations.

item.title: Apple apparently tested a stylus for the foldable iPhone, then nixed the idea (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple reportedly explored and even prototyped a smaller Apple Pencil designed for the upcoming foldable iPhone Ultra, with plans for magnetic attachment and charging similar to the iPad. However, the company apparently abandoned the idea because a stylus could interfere with the folding mechanism and potentially damage the softer surface of the foldable display. While an Apple Pencil is unlikely to launch alongside the first-generation foldable iPhone, the concept may return in future models if foldable screen technology becomes more durable.

item.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash Lets You Build with More Control (2 minute read)
item.description: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash gives developers more control over AI-generated video, moving the model closer to a production-ready creative tool rather than a simple video generator. The update can extend existing scenes while maintaining visual and narrative consistency, generate smooth transitions between specified first and last frames, and use video references to preserve characters and motion. It also adds faster, lower-cost 360p drafts for experimentation and upscaling to 1080p or 4K for finished work.

item.title: Apple will be launching its first pair of smart glasses next year: Here's what's coming (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple is reportedly preparing AI-powered smart glasses for launch in 2027 that focus on voice and camera-based assistance rather than augmented reality displays. The glasses would use Siri and Visual Intelligence to analyze the user's surroundings, answer questions, provide context, translate signs, and save visual reminders, while also functioning as open-ear audio devices. Apple is developing multiple frame styles and premium finishes in-house, with future versions potentially adding health features such as heart-rate monitoring. Unlike Meta's smart glasses, Apple may limit photo and video capture due to privacy concerns. Current reports suggest the product will be unveiled at WWDC 2027 before shipping later that year.

item.title: Rethinking Data Visualization: A UX Approach to Dashboards That Actually Drives Decisions (16 minute read)
item.description: Roughly 80% of what determines whether a dashboard succeeds happens before any chart is drawn, in defining context, audience and the intended insight. Dashboards fail not because the data is thin but because nobody designed them to answer a specific operational question. A B2B talent-management project shows how radar charts, product-coded color, and a comparison view turned passive reporting into weekly planning.

item.title: AI Can't Replace Real Research in Empathy Mapping (5 minute read)
item.description: Empathy maps are most valuable when they are built from real user research, such as interviews, usability testing, support tickets, and field observations. While AI can generate believable user quotes, emotions, and behaviors, these outputs are assumptions rather than evidence and often lack the specific context that reveals genuine user needs and pain points. AI is best used to organize, cluster, summarize, and synthesize existing research data, not to invent users or fill gaps where research is missing. Relying on AI-generated empathy-map content can create a false sense of understanding and lead teams to make decisions based on fictional users instead of real-world insights.

item.title: AI-Generated Images Can Perform as Well as Stock Photography (7 minute read)
item.description: In a study of 77 participants rating a fictional consulting firm's webpage, AI-generated hero images produced no perception penalty against real stock photos. Ratings for trustworthiness, professionalism, and authenticity were slightly higher for the AI images, though only the authenticity difference reached statistical significance, by 0.4 points. Participants who suspected AI involvement rated pages less favorably, and perceived diversity and representation shaped impressions more than image source.

item.title: On Unfurling Interfaces (7 minute read)
item.description: Small interface surfaces work better when they unfold from the edge or control that caused them, rather than arriving through a generic fade and scale. The closed state is a narrow seam built with an inset clip path that preserves the surface's own radius, so corners never square off mid-reveal. Components share a small motion language while keeping their own placement, accessibility, and native lifecycle.

item.title: What Critical Thinking Means for Senior Designers (and How to Apply It) (5 minute read)
item.description: As AI tools put design output within everyone's reach, the senior designer's job shifts from producing the artifact to justifying it in language non-designers can act on. Spotting that a Figma Make mockup breaks is craft - critical thinking is translating that feeling into behavioral and business consequences. Ask what path a screen requires of the user, then what competes with it.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama: The Japanese Avant-Garde Artist Who Created a New Genre of Immersive Art (1 minute read)
item.description: Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama's polka dots, nets, and Infinity Mirror Rooms created a genre of immersive art and inspired the minimalist and Pop Art movements.

item.title: Gabriel Diogo on football, memory, and the warm colors of Brazil's backyards (2 minute read)
item.description: Brazilian illustrator Gabriel Diogo left an unfulfilling design career to pursue illustration full-time, building a distinctive style inspired by Brazilian football culture, everyday life, and community identity, ultimately leading to work with brands like Nike while staying rooted in his personal story and creative values.

item.title: Google's Gemini Has a Branding Problem, and so Does the Rest of AI (3 minute read)
item.description: Google has given nearly every Gemini feature its own brand, cluttering the app and undercutting its own ease-of-use promise.

item.title: Gamma Acquires Accel-Backed Design Startup Lica (3 minute read)
item.description: Presentation startup Gamma has acquired Accel-backed Lica to build a design research lab, which Lica's co-founders will lead. Lica raised $4 million in 2024 and worked with e-commerce sites on brand-compliant marketing videos. Gamma now wants to explore fluid, multimodal presentation formats through the new division.

item.title: The Xiaomi 18 Fold leaks, ahead of the iPhone Ultra launch (1 minute read)
item.description: The smartphone industry appears to be coalescing around the book-style foldable design, where a phone unfolds into a small tablet, rather than the flip-phone format that folds a standard phone in half. Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold, Apple's rumored iPhone Ultra, and leaked images of Xiaomi's upcoming 18 Fold all point to growing momentum behind larger-screen foldables, suggesting that this form factor is emerging as the preferred direction for premium folding phones.

item.title: Adobe Brings ACR's Powerful Non-Destructive Exposure Tools Into Photoshop Itself (3 minute read)
item.description: Adobe has released a major Photoshop update focused on making image editing faster and more intuitive, with new features including a Light Adjustment Layer that brings Camera Raw-style lighting controls directly into Photoshop, Firefly-powered editing tools that can automatically mask and modify specific parts of an image from text instructions, and AI Markup tools for visually communicating edit requests. The update also introduces a beta AI-Assisted Editor, allowing users to make complex edits through natural-language prompts while Photoshop automatically selects and combines the appropriate tools. Adobe says the goal is to let creators spend less time navigating software and more time focusing on creative decisions.

item.title: The Product Designer's Role Isn't Disappearing. It's Getting Weirder (9 minute read)
item.description: AI is collapsing the traditional boundaries between product design, product management, and engineering, making the old handoff-based workflow increasingly obsolete. As AI tools can now turn ideas, requirements, and design systems into working prototypes and code, designers are being pushed toward a broader role the author calls a product architect—someone who combines product thinking, systems design, technical understanding, and creative judgment. Rather than focusing on screens, specs, or deliverables, the most valuable skill becomes deciding what should be built, how it should work, and whether it solves a real problem. This can be an opportunity rather than a threat: design isn't disappearing, but evolving into a more strategic, multidisciplinary role where taste, judgment, and systems thinking matter more than execution.

item.title: The Creativity We Outsource — AI, Creativity and the Lost Value of Doing Things Yourself (6 minute read)
item.description: Generative AI can deliver a solution before there is time to explore the problem, removing the detours where creative learning actually happens. Photoshop began stripping away that friction. AI takes it much further, especially for students and young designers. The proposal is not banning AI but designing for Learning Experience alongside User Experience.

item.title: Speaking Design at Scale (4 minute read)
item.description: Design system pattern names like Overview and PageHeader are shorthand for decisions a team should not have to reopen every time. Learning that vocabulary takes a person months, but an agent can read the repository and retrieve the code, guidance, and examples behind each name. That lets more people describe a screen in the system's own language and judge the result.

item.title: Perfection is Not Over-Engineering (3 minute read)
item.description: Over-engineering means solving the wrong problem, not caring too much, or building something too good. With every constraint on the table, only one solution fits, and that solution is the perfect one. Over-engineering is therefore a failure of requirements gathering, and systems need treating as products with real users.

item.title: The CBI's latest AI report on how design businesses can bridge AI's execution divide (4 minute read)
item.description: The real value of AI now comes from integrating it into core business operations rather than running isolated experiments. Design teams benefit most when AI supports entire workflows from concept creation to production. AI's biggest near-term impact is augmenting human work rather than replacing it, making skills like judgment, creativity, and critical thinking even more important. Automation is reducing traditional entry-level design tasks, creating a risk to the future talent pipeline unless companies redesign junior roles around AI-assisted workflows while also addressing growing legal and copyright concerns around AI-generated work.

item.title: Animation is Having a Punk Rock Moment – And it Says a Lot About How People View AI (5 minute read)
item.description: Niu Lai, a nearly zero-budget animated film made largely by a Chinese mother and son on second-hand computers, has become an unexpected box office hit. Made by former interior designer Xin Yumeng over five years, the crude, low-quality animation grossed over ¥25.67 million despite starting with almost no publicity or earnings. Its success is framed as a reaction against polished, AI-generated visuals, echoing how punk rock once rebelled against overproduced music.

item.title: Calendly Gets a Rippling, Gloopy Rebrand for the AI Age (6 minute read)
item.description: Calendly has unveiled a new logo, wordmark, and color system alongside an AI email assistant and an AI meeting notetaker. The rebrand replaces the previous neon palette with soft prismatic gradients and a rippling "gloop" motif, signaling that the product is more than a scheduling link as AI reshapes productivity software.

item.title: Google Clock and Pixel Magnifier roll out icon redesigns (2 minute read)
item.description: Google has refreshed the Clock and Pixel Magnifier app icons as part of the visual design language introduced with the Pixel 11. The new Clock icon features thicker, watch-inspired hands, a blue gradient face, and a white background that aligns it with Google's broader app ecosystem, while Pixel Magnifier receives a similar treatment with a thicker gradient magnifying glass and updated Quick Settings icon. These changes are purely cosmetic, with no notable updates to the apps' functionality or user interfaces.

item.title: Ads have landed in Apple Maps, and they are as bad as expected (1 minute read)
item.description: Apple has begun rolling out ads in Apple Maps across the US and Canada, showing sponsored locations before and after searches. While Apple says the ads are privacy-focused and don't use personal tracking, critics argue they still risk undermining Apple's privacy reputation and make its premium products feel less premium by introducing advertising into built-in apps.

item.title: The Ledger of Design (4 minute read)
item.description: AI has made finished-looking output cheap, so credibility at work now rests on the trail behind an artifact rather than the artifact itself. Contributors, managers, and agents each need a different ledger: rejected directions, decision rationale, and scoped, reviewable execution. A useful one captures itself from tools already in use and records only what explains how the work came to be.

item.title: Designing Memory (15 minute read)
item.description: The first version of ChatGPT memory was a simple notepad the model could read from, write to, and edit across conversations. The hard part was not the interface, but training the decision boundaries for what is worth saving and when to recall it. Most current memory implementations still over-apply what they know, which makes productive forgetting the missing capability.

item.title: Apple's folding iPhone Ultra could have one fatal flaw for creatives (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's rumored foldable “iPhone Ultra” is reportedly impressing early testers with its pocket-friendly design, durable hinge, and larger iPad-like internal display, potentially making it Apple's most exciting hardware launch in years. However, leaks suggest it may omit key premium features such as a telephoto camera and Face ID, raising questions about its value at a rumored $2,000 price point. For creatives, the choice may come down to whether a larger foldable screen is more important than having Apple's best camera system.

item.title: The Discipline Loop: How Training Rewired My Design Brain (6 minute read)
item.description: Gym training habits transfer to design work as fixed routines that remove hesitation before uncertain effort begins. Timed idea sprints break blank-canvas paralysis, while finishing the rep means named layers, documented states, and handoff-ready files. Polished interfaces that collapse under real data are the design equivalent of an athlete whose gear outpaces actual capacity.

item.title: The boring screens that run the world: a designer's case study (10 minute read)
item.description: A fintech company significantly reduced costly loan-processing errors by redesigning an internal verification screen, highlighting how small usability improvements in back-office tools can have outsized business impact. Internal systems like admin portals, dashboards, compliance tools, and operational software are often more consequential than customer-facing apps, yet receive far less design attention. Some of the most valuable design work lies in understanding complex workflows, supporting decision-making under pressure, and improving the systems that keep businesses running.

item.description: Apple's redesigned Safari icon in iOS 27 has sparked criticism from design enthusiasts, who argue its compass graphic inaccurately resembles two overlapping needles and reflects a decline in Apple's attention to detail.
